decisions.reason: As a newly launched drain housing closely tied to the firm's core drainage technology and modular system logic, it is still an inexpensive option to keep open while market acceptance becomes clearer.

A floor-level shower drainage system fits the firm's strategic move toward integrated, accessible bathroom solutions, so management would likely continue observing uptake rather than abandon it after only one year.
Because the firm presents this designer shower drainage product as a flagship aligned with its future direction, it is very unlikely to be withdrawn before its strategic value is tested further.

The shower element with integrated slope complements the firm's installation-focused offering and should be retained as a promising adjacent option until more evidence on demand and installer adoption emerges.
The backflow-protected basement floor drain addresses a clear technical problem in the firm's core application area, making it worthwhile to keep on the market while its niche demand is assessed.

Although the air-admittance valve is somewhat less central to the firm's design-led shower drainage focus, it still leverages sanitary drainage know-how and is likely to be kept for another year unless early demand proves weak.
